import Mathlib
import Catalog.Geometry.HolographicCode.AreaEntropy

namespace Catalog.Geometry.HolographicCode

open Finset

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis: the standard information-theoretic quantities I(A:B) and I(A:B|C),
--   when DEFINED purely from the geometric area functional `cut`, should be
--   forced nonnegative by the geometry alone.
-- Experiment: set I(A:B) = S A + S B - S(A∪B) and I(A:B|C) = S(A∪C)+S(B∪C)
--   -S(A∪B∪C)-S C, then reduce their nonnegativity to `cut_subadditive` and
--   `cut_submodular`.
-- Result: Confirmed. I(A:B) ≥ 0 is literally subadditivity. I(A:B|C) ≥ 0 is
--   submodularity applied to the pair (A∪C, B∪C): the union is A∪B∪C and, for
--   DISJOINT A,B, the intersection (A∪C)∩(B∪C) = C, giving exactly SSA.
-- Insight: the set identity (A∪C)∩(B∪C) = (A∩B)∪C is the algebraic heart of the
--   "strong subadditivity from geometry" statement; disjointness of A,B is what
--   makes the conditional mutual information land precisely on the C-cut.
-- Failure analysis: without `Disjoint A B`, (A∪C)∩(B∪C) acquires the extra
--   piece A∩B, so the clean identity I(A:B|C) ≥ 0 needs that hypothesis (as in
--   the physical statement for disjoint subsystems).

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- The **mutual information** `I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(A∪B)` read off from the
geometric area functional. -/
def mutualInfo (w : V → V → ℝ) (A B : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  cut w A + cut w B - cut w (A ∪ B)

/-- The **conditional mutual information** `I(A:B|C)` read off from geometry. -/
def condMutualInfo (w : V → V → ℝ) (A B C : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  cut w (A ∪ C) + cut w (B ∪ C) - cut w (A ∪ B ∪ C) - cut w C

/-- Mutual information is nonnegative: the geometric form of **subadditivity**. -/
theorem mutualInfo_nonneg {w : V → V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ u v, 0 ≤ w u v) (A B : Finset V) :
    0 ≤ mutualInfo w A B := by
  have := cut_subadditive hw A B
  unfold mutualInfo
  linarith

/-- Mutual information is symmetric. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comm (w : V → V → ℝ) (A B : Finset V) :
    mutualInfo w A B = mutualInfo w B A := by
  unfold mutualInfo
  rw [Finset.union_comm A B]
  ring

/-- Conditioning on the empty region recovers the plain mutual information. -/
theorem condMutualInfo_zero (w : V → V → ℝ) (A B : Finset V) :
    condMutualInfo w A B ∅ = mutualInfo w A B := by
  unfold condMutualInfo mutualInfo
  simp

/-
Conditional mutual information is nonnegative for disjoint `A, B`: the
geometric form of **strong subadditivity**.
-/
theorem condMutualInfo_nonneg {w : V → V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ u v, 0 ≤ w u v)
    {A B : Finset V} (C : Finset V) (hAB : Disjoint A B) :
    0 ≤ condMutualInfo w A B C := by
  unfold condMutualInfo;
  rw [ show A ∪ B ∪ C = ( A ∪ C ) ∪ ( B ∪ C ) by ext; aesop ];
  convert sub_nonneg_of_le ( cut_submodular hw ( A ∪ C ) ( B ∪ C ) ) using 1;
  rw [ show ( A ∪ C ) ∩ ( B ∪ C ) = C by ext x; by_cases ha : x ∈ A <;> by_cases hb : x ∈ B <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.disjoint_left ] ] ; ring

-- NEW_FILE: 5f9a16a6_retry1_aristotle/Logic/FiniteArgumentationTopology.lean
import Mathlib

/-!
# The topology of finite argumentation frameworks via conflict-free sets

This file formalizes the simplicial-complex structure attached to a finite Dung
argumentation framework `AF = (A, R)`, represented by a (finite) type `α` of
arguments together with a binary attack relation `attacks : α → α → Prop`.

## Main contents

* `ConflictFree attacks S` : `S` is conflict-free, i.e. no two of its members
  (including an element with itself) are related by `attacks`.
* `conflictFree_isSimplicial` : the family `K_cf(AF)` of conflict-free sets is a
  simplicial complex (it is closed under taking subsets).
* `preferred_not_simplicial` : **refutation of the original conjecture.** The
  family of *preferred extensions* (maximal admissible sets) is **not** a
  simplicial complex in general; a one-attack-free framework on two arguments is
  an explicit counterexample, because the unique preferred extension is the whole
  set while its proper subsets are admissible but not preferred (hence not
  downward closed).
* `conflictGraph attacks` : the undirected conflict graph `G(AF)`.
* `conflictFree_iff_isIndepSet` : **central theorem.** Conflict-free sets are
  exactly the independent sets of the conflict graph, so `K_cf(AF)` is the
  independence complex of `G(AF)` (under the standard assumption that no argument
  attacks itself).
* structural theorems: singletons are faces, the 2-element face criterion, facets
  vs. maximal independent sets, the cone over an isolated argument, and a
  product-style (join) characterization for disjoint unions.
* explicit computations: a mutual-attack pair, a directed 3-cycle (conflict graph
  `K₃`), and an edgeless framework (full simplex).

Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsIndepSet` is reused for the independence complex; no
auxiliary graph theory needs to be developed.
-/

namespace FiniteArgFramework

variable {α β : Type*}

/-! ## Conflict-free sets and the simplicial complex `K_cf` -/

/-- A finite set `S` of arguments is **conflict-free** when no two of its members
(including an argument with itself) are related by `attacks`. -/
def ConflictFree (attacks : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, ¬ attacks a b

/-- A family of finite sets is a **simplicial complex** (as a face system) when it
is closed under taking subsets. -/
def IsSimplicialFamily (F : Finset α → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ S, F S → ∀ T, T ⊆ S → F T

/-- Conflict-freeness is downward closed: subsets of conflict-free sets are
conflict-free. -/
theorem ConflictFree.subset {attacks : α → α → Prop} {S T : Finset α}
    (h : ConflictFree attacks S) (hTS : T ⊆ S) : ConflictFree attacks T := by
  exact fun a ha b hb => h a (hTS ha) b (hTS hb)

/-- The family `K_cf(AF)` of conflict-free sets is a simplicial complex. -/
theorem conflictFree_isSimplicial (attacks : α → α → Prop) :
    IsSimplicialFamily (ConflictFree attacks) := by
  exact fun S hS T hTS => ConflictFree.subset hS hTS

/-! ## Admissibility and preferred extensions -/

/-- `S` defends an argument `a` if every attacker of `a` is itself attacked by a
member of `S`. -/
def Defends (attacks : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) (a : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ b, attacks b a → ∃ c ∈ S, attacks c b

/-- A set is **admissible** when it is conflict-free and defends all its members. -/
def Admissible (attacks : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ConflictFree attacks S ∧ ∀ a ∈ S, Defends attacks S a

/-- A **preferred extension** is an inclusion-maximal admissible set. -/
def IsPreferred (attacks : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  Admissible attacks S ∧ ∀ T, Admissible attacks T → S ⊆ T → T = S

/-! ## Refutation of the original conjecture

The original conjecture claimed that the preferred extensions of an argumentation
framework form a simplicial complex on `A`. This is false: preferred extensions
are *maximal* admissible sets, and maximality is not preserved under taking
subsets.

We exhibit the simplest counterexample: the framework on two arguments with no
attacks at all. Every subset is admissible, so the unique preferred extension is
the full set `{0, 1}`, while the proper subset `{0}` is admissible but **not**
preferred. -/

/-- The empty (attack-free) relation on `Fin 2`. -/
def noAttack₂ : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Prop := fun _ _ => False

instance : DecidableRel noAttack₂ := fun _ _ => inferInstanceAs (Decidable False)

/-- The full set is a preferred extension of the attack-free framework. -/
theorem isPreferred_univ_noAttack₂ :
    IsPreferred noAttack₂ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2)) := by
  simp only [IsPreferred, Admissible, Defends, ConflictFree, noAttack₂]
  decide

/-- The proper subset `{0}` is admissible but is *not* a preferred extension. -/
theorem not_isPreferred_singleton_noAttack₂ :
    ¬ IsPreferred noAttack₂ ({0} : Finset (Fin 2)) := by
  simp only [IsPreferred, Admissible, Defends, ConflictFree, noAttack₂]
  decide

/-- **Refutation.** The family of preferred extensions is not a simplicial
complex in general. -/
theorem preferred_not_simplicial :
    ¬ IsSimplicialFamily (IsPreferred noAttack₂) := by
  intro h
  exact not_isPreferred_singleton_noAttack₂
    (h Finset.univ isPreferred_univ_noAttack₂ {0} (Finset.subset_univ _))

/-! ## The conflict graph and the independence complex -/

/-- The undirected **conflict graph** `G(AF)`: there is an edge between distinct
arguments `a` and `b` whenever one attacks the other. -/
def conflictGraph (attacks : α → α → Prop) : SimpleGraph α where
  Adj a b := a ≠ b ∧ (attacks a b ∨ attacks b a)
  symm := fun _ _ ⟨h1, h2⟩ => ⟨fun h => h1 h.symm, h2.symm⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.1 rfl⟩

@[simp] theorem conflictGraph_adj (attacks : α → α → Prop) (a b : α) :
    (conflictGraph attacks).Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ (attacks a b ∨ attacks b a) := Iff.rfl

/-
**Central theorem.** For a framework without self-attacks, the conflict-free
sets are exactly the independent sets of the conflict graph. Hence `K_cf(AF)` is
the independence complex of `G(AF)`.
-/
theorem conflictFree_iff_isIndepSet (attacks : α → α → Prop)
    (hirr : ∀ a, ¬ attacks a a) (S : Finset α) :
    ConflictFree attacks S ↔ (conflictGraph attacks).IsIndepSet (↑S : Set α) := by
  constructor <;> intro h1 <;> simp_all +decide [ Set.Pairwise ];
  · exact fun x hx y hy hxy => ⟨ h1 x hx y hy, h1 y hy x hx ⟩;
  · exact fun a ha b hb => by by_cases hab : a = b <;> aesop;

/-! ## Structural theorems -/

/-
Every singleton is a face (provided no argument attacks itself).
-/
theorem conflictFree_singleton {attacks : α → α → Prop}
    (hirr : ∀ a, ¬ attacks a a) (a : α) : ConflictFree attacks {a} := by
  exact fun x hx y hy => by aesop;

/-
A two-element set `{a, b}` is a face iff neither argument attacks the other.
-/
theorem conflictFree_pair {attacks : α → α → Prop} [DecidableEq α]
    (hirr : ∀ a, ¬ attacks a a) (a b : α) :
    ConflictFree attacks {a, b} ↔ ¬ attacks a b ∧ ¬ attacks b a := by
  constructor;
  · intro h
    unfold ConflictFree at h
    aesop;
  · intro h x hx y hy; aesop;

/-- A **facet** of `K_cf(AF)` is an inclusion-maximal conflict-free set. -/
def IsFacet (attacks : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ConflictFree attacks S ∧ ∀ T, ConflictFree attacks T → S ⊆ T → T = S

/-
Facets of `K_cf(AF)` are exactly the inclusion-maximal independent sets of the
conflict graph (no self-attacks assumed).
-/
theorem isFacet_iff_maximal_indep {attacks : α → α → Prop}
    (hirr : ∀ a, ¬ attacks a a) (S : Finset α) :
    IsFacet attacks S ↔
      (conflictGraph attacks).IsIndepSet (↑S : Set α) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset α, (conflictGraph attacks).IsIndepSet (↑T : Set α) → S ⊆ T → T = S := by
  constructor <;> intro h <;> simp_all +decide [ IsFacet, conflictFree_iff_isIndepSet ]

/-- An argument `a` is **isolated** when it neither attacks nor is attacked by any
argument. -/
def Isolated (attacks : α → α → Prop) (a : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ b, ¬ attacks a b ∧ ¬ attacks b a

/-
**Cone.** If `a` is isolated then adding `a` to any face yields a face. Thus
`K_cf(AF)` is a cone with apex `a`, and is contractible at the combinatorial
level.
-/
theorem conflictFree_insert_isolated {attacks : α → α → Prop} [DecidableEq α]
    {a : α} (ha : Isolated attacks a) {S : Finset α} (hS : ConflictFree attacks S) :
    ConflictFree attacks (insert a S) := by
  grind +locals

/-! ## Disjoint unions and joins -/

/-- The attack relation on the disjoint union of two frameworks: each component
keeps its own attacks and there are no attacks across components. -/
def sumAttack (atA : α → α → Prop) (atB : β → β → Prop) :
    α ⊕ β → α ⊕ β → Prop
  | Sum.inl a, Sum.inl a' => atA a a'
  | Sum.inr b, Sum.inr b' => atB b b'
  | _, _ => False

/-
**Join / product-style characterization.** A set of arguments in a disjoint
union is conflict-free iff its left and right parts are each conflict-free; this
exhibits `K_cf` of a disjoint union as the join of the component complexes.
-/
theorem conflictFree_sum {atA : α → α → Prop} {atB : β → β → Prop}
    (S : Finset (α ⊕ β)) :
    ConflictFree (sumAttack atA atB) S ↔
      (∀ a a', Sum.inl a ∈ S → Sum.inl a' ∈ S → ¬ atA a a') ∧
      (∀ b b', Sum.inr b ∈ S → Sum.inr b' ∈ S → ¬ atB b b') := by
  unfold ConflictFree sumAttack;
  grind

/-! ## Small explicit examples -/

/-! ### Edgeless framework: the full simplex -/

/-- In an attack-free framework every set is conflict-free: `K_cf` is the full
simplex. -/
theorem conflictFree_noAttack₂ (S : Finset (Fin 2)) : ConflictFree noAttack₂ S := by
  simp only [ConflictFree, noAttack₂]; revert S; decide

/-! ### A mutual-attack pair -/

/-- A pair of arguments that attack each other (and have no self-attacks),
modelled on `Fin 2` by the inequality relation. -/
def mutualAttack : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Prop := fun a b => a ≠ b

instance : DecidableRel mutualAttack := fun a b => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a ≠ b))

/-- The conflict graph of a mutual-attack pair is the complete graph `K₂`. -/
theorem conflictGraph_mutualAttack :
    conflictGraph mutualAttack = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  ext a b
  simp only [conflictGraph_adj, SimpleGraph.top_adj, mutualAttack]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h, _⟩; exact h
  · intro h; exact ⟨h, Or.inl h⟩

/-- For a mutual-attack pair the faces of `K_cf` are exactly the sets of size at
most one: two vertices `{0}`, `{1}`, the empty face, and **no edge**. -/
theorem conflictFree_mutualAttack_iff (S : Finset (Fin 2)) :
    ConflictFree mutualAttack S ↔ S.card ≤ 1 := by
  simp only [ConflictFree, mutualAttack]; revert S; decide

/-! ### A directed 3-cycle -/

/-- The directed 3-cycle `0 → 1 → 2 → 0` on `Fin 3`. -/
def cycle₃ : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Prop := fun a b =>
  (a = 0 ∧ b = 1) ∨ (a = 1 ∧ b = 2) ∨ (a = 2 ∧ b = 0)

instance : DecidableRel cycle₃ := fun a b =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable ((a = 0 ∧ b = 1) ∨ (a = 1 ∧ b = 2) ∨ (a = 2 ∧ b = 0)))

/-- The conflict graph of the directed 3-cycle is the complete graph `K₃`. -/
theorem conflictGraph_cycle₃ : conflictGraph cycle₃ = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  ext a b
  simp only [conflictGraph_adj, SimpleGraph.top_adj, cycle₃]
  revert a b; decide

/-- For the directed 3-cycle the faces of `K_cf` are exactly `∅` and the
singletons: the complex consists only of the empty set and the vertices. -/
theorem conflictFree_cycle₃_iff (S : Finset (Fin 3)) :
    ConflictFree cycle₃ S ↔ S.card ≤ 1 := by
  simp only [ConflictFree, cycle₃]; revert S; decide

end FiniteArgFramework

# Future Directions — The Topology of Argumentation: Why Debates Have Holes

This cycle established a formal core for abstract argumentation frameworks (AFs) in
`Catalog/Novelty/ArgumentationTopology.lean`:

- the **lattice / fixed-point backbone** (`charF_mono`, `grounded`, `grounded_fixed`,
  `grounded_least`) — the canonical "skeleton" of a debate via Knaster–Tarski;
- the **Dung hierarchy** `stable ⟹ complete ⟹ admissible` (`stable_admissible`,
  `stable_complete`, `admissible_empty`);
- the two fundamental **holes** — the odd cycle `cyc3` and the self-loop `loop1` — versus
  the resolvable even cycle `cyc2`, with a `Finset ↔ Set` bridge (`hole_cyc3`,
  `hole_loop1`, `resolvable_cyc2`, `hole_cyc3_set`);
- the structural insight that **holes require asymmetry**: every finite *symmetric,
  irreflexive* debate is resolvable (`symmetric_irreflexive_resolvable`).

The following conjectures are bold, precise, and testable in subsequent cycles.

## C1 — The Parity Theorem for directed cycles
For the directed `n`-cycle `cyc n : Fin n → Fin n → Prop := fun i j => j = i + 1`,
a stable extension exists **iff `n` is even** (`n ≥ 2`):
```
theorem cyc_resolvable_iff_even (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    Resolvable (cyc n) ↔ Even n
```
We verified `n = 2` (resolvable) and `n = 3` (hole). The conjecture promotes "the odd hole"
from an example to a theorem: parity of a directed cycle is *the* topological invariant
governing resolvability. Likely proof: stable extensions of `cyc n` are exactly the
alternating independent sets, which exist iff `n` is even.

## C2 — Grounded extension is always complete (and conflict-free)
The least fixed point `grounded r` should itself be a genuine extension:
```
theorem grounded_complete (r : A → A → Prop) : Complete r (grounded r)
theorem grounded_conflictFree (r : A → A → Prop) : ConflictFree r (grounded r)
```
This would show every debate has a canonical (possibly empty) "forced core" that is a real
position, even when no stable extension exists — i.e. the skeleton survives even in holed
debates. The expected proof uses `OrderHom.lfp` induction (`lfp_induction`) with
conflict-freeness as the invariant; the subtlety is that conflict-freeness is not
obviously preserved by `charF`, so an auxiliary invariant (admissibility of the iterates)
is likely needed.

## C3 — Euler-characteristic / Betti obstruction (the homological hole count)
Make the topology literal. Associate to a finite AF `r` the directed graph and a chain
complex whose first Betti number `b₁` counts independent directed cycles. Conjecture: a
finite AF with `b₁ = 0` (a "forest of attacks") is always resolvable, and more strongly the
*number of distinct holes* (maximal sub-debates with no stable extension) is bounded by a
function of `b₁`:
```
def b1 (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) : ℕ := ...   -- cycle rank of the attack digraph
theorem acyclic_resolvable (r : Fin n → Fin n → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (h : b1 r = 0) : Resolvable r
```
This is the sharpest sense of "why debates have holes": holes are detected by first
homology of the attack complex. A natural first milestone: prove that an attack relation
that is a strict partial order (well-founded, acyclic) always has a stable extension equal
to its grounded extension.

## C4 — Stability gap = obstruction class
Define the *stability gap* of a debate as the minimal number of arguments that must be
deleted to make it resolvable. Conjecture: for symmetric+irreflexive AFs the gap is `0`
(C-confirmed direction), and for a directed `n`-cycle the gap is exactly `1` when `n` is
odd. More generally the gap equals the minimum number of vertices meeting every "odd
attack cycle", an argumentation analogue of the odd-cycle transversal / `χ`-boundedness
phenomenon.

## C5 — Continuity / sheaf gluing of local debates
Treat a large debate as glued from overlapping sub-debates (a cover). Conjecture: if every
member of a cover is resolvable and the resolutions agree on overlaps (a *cocycle*
condition), then the global debate is resolvable; the obstruction to gluing lives in an
`H¹` of the nerve of the cover. This would turn "debates have holes" into a genuine
sheaf-cohomological statement and connect the Novelty catalog to the persistent-homology
and sheaf entries in the Tropical catalog.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Tropical/Persistence/SublevelFiltration.lean
import Mathlib

/-!
# Tropical Persistent Topology: Sublevel Filtrations of Tropical Polynomials

This file develops a *topological-data-analysis* (TDA) view of tropical polynomials.
A **tropical polynomial** on `ℝⁿ` is a finite max-plus combination of affine
"monomials"
`monomial aᵢ bᵢ (x) = aᵢ + ⟨bᵢ, x⟩`,
its value function being `p.toFun x = ⨆ᵢ (aᵢ + ⟨bᵢ, x⟩)`.

The central object of study is the **sublevel filtration**
`sublevel p c = { x | p.toFun x ≤ c }`,
the basic input to persistent homology.  We prove that this filtration is
*as topologically trivial as possible* in degree 0: every sublevel set is convex,
hence preconnected, the filtration is monotone, and the family of thresholds with
nonempty sublevel set is upward closed.  Consequently the degree-0 persistence
diagram is a **single bar** `[birth, ∞)` — there is no merging or splitting of
connected components, ever.

We also show that the class of tropical polynomials is closed under the two
semiring operations, and that these operations act on value functions exactly as
the tropical semiring `(ℝ, max, +)` predicts:

* `toFun_tropAdd`  : `(p ⊕ q).toFun = max (p.toFun) (q.toFun)`  (tropical `+`)
* `toFun_tropMul`  : `(p ⊗ q).toFun = p.toFun + q.toFun`        (tropical `·`)
* `toFun_distrib`  : distributivity of `⊗` over `⊕`.

This connects the catalog's `Tropical/Core/TropicalSemiringProperties.lean`
(pointwise identities for `max`/`+`) to the *geometric/topological* layer.

## Main results

* `convexOn_toFun`            — tropical polynomials are convex functions.
* `convex_sublevel`           — every sublevel set is convex.
* `sublevel_mono`             — the filtration is monotone (a genuine filtration).
* `isPreconnected_sublevel`   — every sublevel set is preconnected.
* `isConnected_sublevel`      — every nonempty sublevel set is connected.
* `H0_single_bar`             — the degree-0 persistence is a single bar.
* `nonempty_sublevel_upward`  — the birth set of thresholds is upward closed.
* `toFun_tropAdd` / `toFun_tropMul` / `toFun_distrib` — tropical algebra of values.
* `toFun_tropAdd_self`        — tropical idempotence `p ⊕ p ≡ p`.
* `sublevel_tropAdd`          — filtration of a sum is the intersection.

-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace TropicalPersistence

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## Monomials and their convexity -/

/-- A tropical monomial: the affine map `x ↦ a + ⟨b, x⟩`. -/
def monomial (a : ℝ) (b : Fin n → ℝ) : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ := fun x => a + ∑ j, b j * x j

/-- Affine maps are convex, so every tropical monomial is a convex function. -/
theorem convexOn_monomial (a : ℝ) (b : Fin n → ℝ) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (monomial a b) := by
  have hL : IsLinearMap ℝ (fun x : Fin n → ℝ => ∑ j, b j * x j) := by
    constructor
    · intro x y; simp only [Pi.add_apply, mul_add]; rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    · intro c x
      simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => by ring)
  have h1 : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : Fin n → ℝ => ∑ j, b j * x j) :=
    LinearMap.convexOn (IsLinearMap.mk' _ hL) convex_univ
  simpa [monomial, add_comm] using h1.add_const a

/-! ## Tropical polynomials -/

/-- A tropical polynomial on `ℝⁿ`: a finite, nonempty family of affine monomials.
Its value is the pointwise maximum (the tropical sum) of the monomials. -/
structure TropPoly (n : ℕ) where
  ι : Type
  fintypeι : Fintype ι
  nonemptyι : Nonempty ι
  coeff : ι → ℝ
  slope : ι → (Fin n → ℝ)

attribute [instance] TropPoly.fintypeι TropPoly.nonemptyι

/-- The value function of a tropical polynomial: the max over its monomials. -/
def TropPoly.toFun (p : TropPoly n) : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun i => monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i))

theorem TropPoly.toFun_apply (p : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    p.toFun x = Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
      (fun i => monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i) x) := by
  rw [TropPoly.toFun, Finset.sup'_apply]

/-- **Tropical polynomials are convex functions.**  A finite max of convex
functions is convex; here each monomial is affine. -/
theorem convexOn_toFun (p : TropPoly n) : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ p.toFun := by
  apply Finset.sup'_induction
  · intro a ha b hb; exact ha.sup hb
  · intro i _; exact convexOn_monomial _ _

/-! ## The sublevel filtration

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis H1: "Tropical polynomials have topologically trivial sublevel
filtrations in degree 0."  Rationale: a tropical polynomial is convex
(piecewise-linear convex), so each sublevel set is an intersection of finitely
many closed half-spaces — a convex polyhedron, hence contractible whenever
nonempty.  Outcome: confirmed.  `convex_sublevel` follows mechanically from
`ConvexOn.convex_le`, and convexity ⇒ preconnected/connected gives the H0
statement.  No counterexample is possible: convexity is unconditional in the
number of monomials and the dimension `n`.
-/

/-- The sublevel set at threshold `c` — the basic input to persistent homology. -/
def sublevel (p : TropPoly n) (c : ℝ) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) := {x | p.toFun x ≤ c}

theorem mem_sublevel_self (p : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    x ∈ sublevel p (p.toFun x) := by
  show p.toFun x ≤ p.toFun x; exact le_rfl

/-- Each sublevel set is convex. -/
theorem convex_sublevel (p : TropPoly n) (c : ℝ) : Convex ℝ (sublevel p c) := by
  have := (convexOn_toFun p).convex_le c
  convert this using 1; ext x; simp [sublevel]

/-- The sublevel sets form a genuine (monotone) filtration. -/
theorem sublevel_mono (p : TropPoly n) {c c' : ℝ} (h : c ≤ c') :
    sublevel p c ⊆ sublevel p c' := fun _ hx => le_trans hx h

/-- Every sublevel set is preconnected. -/
theorem isPreconnected_sublevel (p : TropPoly n) (c : ℝ) :
    IsPreconnected (sublevel p c) := (convex_sublevel p c).isPreconnected

/-- Every nonempty sublevel set is connected. -/
theorem isConnected_sublevel (p : TropPoly n) (c : ℝ)
    (h : (sublevel p c).Nonempty) : IsConnected (sublevel p c) :=
  (convex_sublevel p c).isConnected h

/-- The set of thresholds with nonempty sublevel set is **upward closed**:
once a connected component is born it never dies. -/
theorem nonempty_sublevel_upward (p : TropPoly n) {c c' : ℝ} (h : c ≤ c')
    (hc : (sublevel p c).Nonempty) : (sublevel p c').Nonempty :=
  hc.mono (sublevel_mono p h)

/-- **Degree-0 persistence is a single bar.**  For any two thresholds `c ≤ c'`
with `sublevel p c` nonempty, both sublevel sets are connected and one includes
the other.  Hence the inclusion induces an isomorphism on `H₀` (a singleton to a
singleton): there is exactly one persistent connected component `[birth, ∞)`,
with no births after the first and no deaths. -/
theorem H0_single_bar (p : TropPoly n) {c c' : ℝ} (h : c ≤ c')
    (hc : (sublevel p c).Nonempty) :
    IsConnected (sublevel p c) ∧ IsConnected (sublevel p c') ∧
      sublevel p c ⊆ sublevel p c' :=
  ⟨isConnected_sublevel p c hc,
   isConnected_sublevel p c' (nonempty_sublevel_upward p h hc),
   sublevel_mono p h⟩

/-! ## Tropical algebra of value functions

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis H2: "The class of tropical polynomials is closed under the tropical
semiring operations, and these operations act on the *value functions* by
`max` and `+` respectively."  This is the bridge from the catalog's pointwise
semiring identities (`Tropical/Core/TropicalSemiringProperties.lean`) to the
structured objects here.

Experiment: define `tropAdd` by concatenating monomial index sets (`p.ι ⊕ q.ι`)
and `tropMul` by taking the product index set (`p.ι × q.ι`) with summed
coefficients/slopes — the tropical product of polynomials.  Verify the value
identities.

Outcome: both confirmed.  `toFun_tropAdd` is proved by antisymmetry using
`Finset.le_sup'`/`Finset.sup'_le` directly on the universal finset (avoiding any
`Finset.univ` union lemma for sum types).  `toFun_tropMul` is the *tropical
distributivity* `(⨆ᵢ uᵢ) + (⨆ⱼ vⱼ) = ⨆_{i,j} (uᵢ + vⱼ)`; the `≥` direction needs
the attainment of the max (`Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup'`).

Failure analysis: an earlier attempt rewrote `toFun` via `Finset.sup'` over the
sum-type universal finset hoping for a `sup'_union` simp; that path required
fiddly `Finset.map`/image lemmas.  Switching to the elementwise
`le_sup'`/`sup'_le` characterization removed the friction entirely.

Insight: idempotence of `⊕` (`toFun_tropAdd_self`) is exactly `max_self` lifted
to polynomials — the structured analogue of the catalog's
`tropical_max_idempotent`.  Likewise `toFun_distrib` lifts
`tropical_scalar_distrib`.
-/

/-- Tropical addition (`⊕`, the pointwise max) of two tropical polynomials. -/
def tropAdd (p q : TropPoly n) : TropPoly n where
  ι := p.ι ⊕ q.ι
  fintypeι := inferInstance
  nonemptyι := inferInstance
  coeff := Sum.elim p.coeff q.coeff
  slope := Sum.elim p.slope q.slope

/-- `⊕` acts on value functions as pointwise `max` (tropical sum). -/
theorem toFun_tropAdd (p q : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropAdd p q).toFun x = max (p.toFun x) (q.toFun x) := by
  rw [TropPoly.toFun_apply, TropPoly.toFun_apply, TropPoly.toFun_apply]
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply Finset.sup'_le
    rintro (i | j) _
    · exact le_max_of_le_left
        (Finset.le_sup' (fun i => monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i) x) (Finset.mem_univ i))
    · exact le_max_of_le_right
        (Finset.le_sup' (fun j => monomial (q.coeff j) (q.slope j) x) (Finset.mem_univ j))
  · apply max_le
    · apply Finset.sup'_le; intro i _
      exact Finset.le_sup'
        (fun k => monomial ((tropAdd p q).coeff k) ((tropAdd p q).slope k) x)
        (Finset.mem_univ (Sum.inl i))
    · apply Finset.sup'_le; intro j _
      exact Finset.le_sup'
        (fun k => monomial ((tropAdd p q).coeff k) ((tropAdd p q).slope k) x)
        (Finset.mem_univ (Sum.inr j))

/-- **Tropical idempotence**: `p ⊕ p` has the same value function as `p`.
The structured analogue of `tropical_max_idempotent`. -/
theorem toFun_tropAdd_self (p : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropAdd p p).toFun x = p.toFun x := by rw [toFun_tropAdd, max_self]

/-- Commutativity of `⊕` on value functions. -/
theorem toFun_tropAdd_comm (p q : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropAdd p q).toFun x = (tropAdd q p).toFun x := by
  rw [toFun_tropAdd, toFun_tropAdd, max_comm]

/-- Tropical multiplication (`⊗`, the polynomial product) of two tropical
polynomials: product index set with summed coefficients and slopes. -/
def tropMul (p q : TropPoly n) : TropPoly n where
  ι := p.ι × q.ι
  fintypeι := inferInstance
  nonemptyι := inferInstance
  coeff := fun ij => p.coeff ij.1 + q.coeff ij.2
  slope := fun ij => p.slope ij.1 + q.slope ij.2

theorem monomial_add (a a' : ℝ) (b b' : Fin n → ℝ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    monomial (a + a') (b + b') x = monomial a b x + monomial a' b' x := by
  simp only [monomial, Pi.add_apply, add_mul]; rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]; ring

/-- `⊗` acts on value functions as pointwise `+` (tropical product).  This is the
tropical distributivity identity `(⨆ uᵢ)+(⨆ vⱼ) = ⨆_{i,j}(uᵢ+vⱼ)`. -/
theorem toFun_tropMul (p q : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropMul p q).toFun x = p.toFun x + q.toFun x := by
  rw [TropPoly.toFun_apply, TropPoly.toFun_apply, TropPoly.toFun_apply]
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply Finset.sup'_le
    intro ij _
    rw [show monomial ((tropMul p q).coeff ij) ((tropMul p q).slope ij) x
        = monomial (p.coeff ij.1) (p.slope ij.1) x + monomial (q.coeff ij.2) (q.slope ij.2) x
        from monomial_add _ _ _ _ x]
    exact add_le_add
      (Finset.le_sup' (fun i => monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i) x) (Finset.mem_univ ij.1))
      (Finset.le_sup' (fun j => monomial (q.coeff j) (q.slope j) x) (Finset.mem_univ ij.2))
  · obtain ⟨i0, _, hi0⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := p.ι))
      (fun i => monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i) x)
    obtain ⟨j0, _, hj0⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := q.ι))
      (fun j => monomial (q.coeff j) (q.slope j) x)
    rw [hi0, hj0, ← monomial_add]
    exact Finset.le_sup'
      (fun ij => monomial ((tropMul p q).coeff ij) ((tropMul p q).slope ij) x)
      (Finset.mem_univ (i0, j0))

/-- Commutativity of `⊗` on value functions. -/
theorem toFun_tropMul_comm (p q : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropMul p q).toFun x = (tropMul q p).toFun x := by
  rw [toFun_tropMul, toFun_tropMul, add_comm]

/-- **Tropical distributivity** of `⊗` over `⊕` at the level of value functions.
Lifts the catalog identity `a + max b c = max (a+b) (a+c)`. -/
theorem toFun_distrib (p q r : TropPoly n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (tropMul p (tropAdd q r)).toFun x
      = (tropAdd (tropMul p q) (tropMul p r)).toFun x := by
  rw [toFun_tropMul, toFun_tropAdd, toFun_tropAdd, toFun_tropMul, toFun_tropMul]
  rcases le_total (q.toFun x) (r.toFun x) with hqr | hqr
  · rw [max_eq_right hqr, max_eq_right (by linarith)]
  · rw [max_eq_left hqr, max_eq_left (by linarith)]

/-! ## Filtration compatibility of tropical operations

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis H3: the tropical operations interact with the persistence filtration
in a controlled way.  Since `⊕` is a max, a point lies in a sublevel set of
`p ⊕ q` iff it lies in *both* sublevel sets — the filtration of a sum is the
intersection of the filtrations.  This is the persistence-theoretic
manifestation of `max ≤ c ↔ (· ≤ c) ∧ (· ≤ c)`.  Confirmed below; it gives a
clean way to read off births of `p ⊕ q` from those of `p` and `q`.
-/

/-- The sublevel set of a tropical sum is the intersection of the sublevel sets:
`sublevel (p ⊕ q) c = sublevel p c ∩ sublevel q c`. -/
theorem sublevel_tropAdd (p q : TropPoly n) (c : ℝ) :
    sublevel (tropAdd p q) c = sublevel p c ∩ sublevel q c := by
  ext x
  simp only [sublevel, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_inter_iff, toFun_tropAdd, max_le_iff]

/-! ## Persistence stability

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis H4 (conjecture C3): the value function depends Lipschitz-continuously
on the coefficients, with constant 1, hence the degree-0 *birth value* is stable
under coefficient perturbations — a tropical bottleneck-stability statement.

Experiment: keep the index set and the slopes fixed, perturb only the
coefficients (`TropPoly.recoeff`).  The slope contribution `⟨bᵢ, x⟩` cancels in
the monomial difference, so `|monomialᵢ(p) − monomialᵢ(p')| = |coeffᵢ − coeff'ᵢ|`
uniformly in `x`.  Combined with the elementary `sup'`-Lipschitz inequality
`|⨆ u − ⨆ v| ≤ ⨆ |u − v|` (`abs_sup'_sub_sup'_le`), this yields a *dimension-free*
bound independent of `x`.

Outcome: confirmed (`toFun_stable`).  The bound is sharp: take a single monomial
(`card ι = 1`) and the two sides are equal.  Insight: stability is exactly the
statement that `p ↦ p.toFun` is short for the sup-metric on coefficients — the
first rung toward the barcode-stability program of C3/C5.
-/

/-- A generic `sup'`-Lipschitz inequality: the sup' is short for the sup-distance.
`|⨆ᵢ uᵢ − ⨆ᵢ vᵢ| ≤ ⨆ᵢ |uᵢ − vᵢ|`. -/
theorem abs_sup'_sub_sup'_le {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) (u v : α → ℝ) :
    |s.sup' hs u - s.sup' hs v| ≤ s.sup' hs (fun i => |u i - v i|) := by
  rw [abs_sub_le_iff]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [sub_le_iff_le_add]
    apply Finset.sup'_le
    intro i hi
    have h1 : v i ≤ s.sup' hs v := Finset.le_sup' v hi
    have h2 : |u i - v i| ≤ s.sup' hs (fun i => |u i - v i|) :=
      Finset.le_sup' (fun i => |u i - v i|) hi
    have h3 := le_abs_self (u i - v i)
    linarith
  · rw [sub_le_iff_le_add]
    apply Finset.sup'_le
    intro i hi
    have h1 : u i ≤ s.sup' hs u := Finset.le_sup' u hi
    have h2 : |u i - v i| ≤ s.sup' hs (fun i => |u i - v i|) :=
      Finset.le_sup' (fun i => |u i - v i|) hi
    have h3 := neg_le_abs (u i - v i)
    linarith

/-- Re-coefficient a tropical polynomial, keeping the index set and slopes. -/
def TropPoly.recoeff (p : TropPoly n) (a' : p.ι → ℝ) : TropPoly n :=
  { p with coeff := a' }

/-- **Persistence stability (Lipschitz value function).**  Perturbing only the
coefficients moves the value function by at most the sup-distance of the
coefficients, *uniformly in* `x`.  This is the pointwise core of barcode
stability for tropical polynomials. -/
theorem toFun_stable (p : TropPoly n) (a' : p.ι → ℝ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    |p.toFun x - (p.recoeff a').toFun x|
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun i => |p.coeff i - a' i|) := by
  rw [TropPoly.toFun_apply, TropPoly.toFun_apply]
  refine le_trans (abs_sup'_sub_sup'_le _ _ _ _) (le_of_eq ?_)
  apply Finset.sup'_congr
  · rfl
  intro i _
  show |monomial (p.coeff i) (p.slope i) x - monomial ((p.recoeff a').coeff i) ((p.recoeff a').slope i) x|
      = |p.coeff i - a' i|
  simp only [TropPoly.recoeff, monomial]
  congr 1
  ring

end TropicalPersistence

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Tropical Persistent Topology

Research cycle: *Topological Data Analysis of Theorem Networks* (Domain: Tropical).
Foundation laid in `Catalog/Tropical/Persistence/SublevelFiltration.lean`:
tropical polynomials are convex, their sublevel filtrations have a single-bar
degree-0 persistence, and the tropical semiring operations `⊕ = max`, `⊗ = +`
act on value functions and on the filtration in a controlled way.

Below are bold, **testable** conjectures for follow-up cycles. Each is stated so
that it can be formalized as a Lean theorem (or refuted by a Lean
counterexample).

## C1 — Degree-`k` persistence collapse (k ≥ 1)
**Conjecture.** For every tropical polynomial `p : TropPoly n` and every threshold
`c`, the sublevel set `sublevel p c` is contractible whenever it is nonempty;
hence *all* reduced persistent homology vanishes and the full persistence diagram
is the single H₀ bar already established.
*Test.* Strengthen `convex_sublevel` to `Contractible`/`StarConvex` (a convex set
in `ℝⁿ` is contractible). Formalize via `Convex.contractibleSpace` or by
exhibiting a star-center. Falsifiable: produce a `p`, `c` with disconnected or
holey sublevel set (impossible if convexity is unconditional — so the conjecture
predicts no such example exists).

## C2 — Tropical hypersurfaces are the true carriers of topology
**Conjecture.** Replace the *sublevel* set by the **tropical hypersurface**
(the non-differentiability locus `V(p) = { x | the max in p.toFun x is attained
≥ twice }`). Then the filtration of `ℝⁿ \ V(p)` by connected components is
governed by `card p.ι`: the number of top-dimensional regions equals the number
of monomials that are "essential" (achieve the max somewhere), and this count is
*sub-additive* under `⊕` and *multiplicative-with-defect* under `⊗`.
*Test.* Define `essential p = { i | ∃ x, p.toFun x = monomial (coeff i) (slope i) x }`
and prove `essential (tropAdd p q) ⊆ image essential p ∪ image essential q`.

## C3 — Persistence stability for tropical polynomials  *(pointwise core: PROVED)*
**Status.** The pointwise, dimension-free part is established as `toFun_stable`
in `SublevelFiltration.lean`: `|p.toFun x − (p.recoeff a').toFun x| ≤
⨆ᵢ |coeffᵢ − a'ᵢ|`, uniformly in `x`, with the generic `sup'`-Lipschitz lemma
`abs_sup'_sub_sup'_le`.
**Remaining conjecture.** Lift this to *barcode* stability: the degree-0 birth
value `b(p)` (see C4) is `1`-Lipschitz in the coefficients, and more generally the
bottleneck distance of persistence diagrams is bounded by the sup-distance of
coefficients.
*Test.* Combine `toFun_stable` with the existence of a minimizer (C4) to bound
`|b(p) − b(q)|`. Falsifiable by any coefficient perturbation producing a
birth-value jump exceeding the perturbation.

## C4 — Newton-polytope ↔ persistence dictionary
**Conjecture.** The birth value `b(p) = inf { c | sublevel p c ≠ ∅ }` of the
single H₀ bar equals the value of the tropical polynomial at the *tropical
minimum*, and is determined entirely by the lower hull of the lifted Newton
polytope `{ (slope i, coeff i) }`. In particular `b(tropMul p q) = b(p) + b(q)`
and `b(tropAdd p q) = min (b(p)) (b(q))` whenever the relevant infima are
attained (e.g. all slopes nonzero / coercive case).
*Test.* Introduce a coercivity hypothesis guaranteeing attainment, prove
existence of a global minimizer (`IsCompact` sublevel sets), then the additive
and min laws for `b` follow from `toFun_tropMul` and `toFun_tropAdd`.

## C5 — Theorem-network functoriality (the meta-TDA layer)
**Conjecture.** Assigning to each tropical polynomial its persistence barcode is
*functorial* over the tropical semiring: there is a barcode-valued semiring
homomorphism sending `⊕` to barcode-min and `⊗` to barcode-sum, extending the
catalog's `TropicalSemiringHom`. Formally, the assignment
`p ↦ b(p) ∈ (ℝ, min, +)` is a semiring homomorphism into the tropical semiring
itself — i.e. tropical persistence is a *self-map of the tropical line*.
*Test.* Once C4 supplies `b`, prove `b` is a `min`-`+` homomorphism, closing the
loop with `Tropical/NeuralNetworks/TropicalSemiringHom.lean`. Falsifiable if any
`p, q` violate `b(p ⊕ q) = min (b p) (b q)`.
